CHECK on the airspace: fine as a play-height envelope over one sea surface, and only a problem if the storms are built as layered volumes the flight passes between
New Zealand to Canada cannot be one framed map at any useful detail; the crossing is built as one representative stretch of ocean and storm unless the user wants it split into legs

handoff.theme: Open ocean and storm sky - grey rough seas, heavy cloud, distant coastlines

open_questions.ask: Is there an end to the flight - you land in Canada and it's over - or does it keep going as long as you can survive?
Is there anywhere to touch down along the way - islands, ships, rocks to rest on - or is it unbroken open water?
How should this look - a bright cartoon duck and toy-like waves, or a grey realistic storm at sea?

captured: a migration from New Zealand to Canada
flying as the means of travel

enriched_invented.detail: a rocky New Zealand shoreline with native vegetation as the starting area
Canadian mountain ranges and forests on the far horizon
breaks of sunlight between storm formations
the whole journey composed as one foreground-to-background scene

notes_for_us: This sits exactly between Adventure and Infinite Runner and the two route differently - open airspace at CHECK versus a genre-wide P6 on chunked segments. The tell the skill offers is whether the course ends, which is the one thing the prompt does not say, so I classified on the destination being named and asked the endless question the skill sanctions.

Storms are the obstacle in this game and hazard-kill was the closest row, which makes them damaging ground regions. A storm is a moving volume of weather you fly through; nothing distinguishes weather-as-obstacle from a lava field, and the same request also has a real claim on the sky consumer.

Flight makes the scale table awkward. The bands are named for things on the ground, and the smallest thing a flying player needs to pick out is a storm cell or a wave crest - neither of which is furniture, a building, a road, or a coastline.

unmatched_options.text: storms flown across as the main obstacle of the migration
rough seas below the flight path
a duck that has to keep flying across an ocean crossing

skill_gap.name: scale bands assume a ground plane
skill_gap.why: the four bands are keyed to ground objects, and a flight game over open water has no furniture, buildings or roads to pick the band from
